mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 3.0% consistently indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance, which reduces discount rates for equity valuation and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS is below 3.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate exceeding 4.5% signals a restrictive monetary policy, which increases equity discount rates and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS is above 4.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) exceeds its 12-month moving average and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.0%, it indicates a strengthening economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 55% of instances where INDPRO > 12mo_MA and UNRATE < 4.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a housing market recovery (HOUST above 1200 and RSAFS above 500000), increased consumer confidence and spending drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances where HOUST > 1200 and RSAFS > 500000, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A declining unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a tightening labor market, which typically increases corporate profit margins and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE is declining, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts rate below 1200 thousand units signals a weakening housing market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to reduced consumer spending and economic growth concerns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of instances where HOUST is below 1200, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When core inflation (CPIAUCSL) rises above 255 and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) remains below 2.5%, it indicates a policy response to inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 255 and FEDFUNDS < 2.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A core inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) above 255 signals persistent inflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the Federal Reserve may tighten policy.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances where CPIAUCSL is above 255, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
